newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana minister urges accelerated privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Botswana minister urges accelerated privatisation.

text.p: The Botswana government should push ahead with privatisation and distribute control of productive assets more widely among the population, said Minister for Mineral Resources and Water Affairs, David Magang.

"The government should accelerate and facilitate the privatisation of many of its operations to empower the indigenous people," Magang told a reception on the further development of Phakalane, a residential and industrial estate on the outskirts of Gaborone.
"Our country is rich, it's people not...They do not participate in the economy, but are simply workers."

Government involvement in all sectors of the economy had been justified in the early days of independence when there was no private sector to speak of, but it was now the time to promote private initiative, he said.

The managing director of the Botswana Confederation of Commerce, Industry and Manpower, Modiri Mbaakanyi, called at the same meeting for a fund to provide capital for indigenous Batswana to set up businesses.
"This rich country should not have poor people. Government should establish a citizen empowerment fund to provide capital for indigenous Batswana-owned businesses," Mbaakanyi said.

The Magang family are the developers of Phakalane, which was their family farm. Magang's son, Lesang, managing director of Phakalane Estates, is also the leader of the ruling Democratic Party (BDP) youth wing.
Finance minister Festus Mogae said last year that the government planned to privatise key state corporations and utilities over the next few years, but no firm timetable has yet been set.
Mogae told Reuters in December that an interdepartmental task force was likely to issue a privatisation policy paper towards the end of 1997.
Diamond-rich and virtually debt-free Botswana is under no budgetary pressure to sell state assets to raise funds.
